title: Relative topos cohomology cone and finite covering comparison
statement:
Let $G$ be a profinite group, $H\subset G$ an open subgroup of finite index, $Q=G/H$, and $A$ a finite commutative ring. Let $BG$ and $BH$ denote the topoi of discrete continuous sets with action of the indicated group; $A$-module objects are as in [def-exc-discrete-modules-category]. Let $E$ be a Grothendieck topos (the category of sheaves on a small site [def-weil-pbc-topos]) and $\rho:E\to BG$ a morphism of topoi (an adjunction with finite-limit-preserving inverse image). Form $E'=E/\rho^*Q$ and the cartesian square
$$\begin{matrix} E'&\xrightarrow{\rho'}&BH\simeq(BG)/Q\\ g\downarrow&&\downarrow g'\\ E&\xrightarrow{\rho}&BG.\end{matrix}$$
All ring sheaves are the constant sheaf $A$, all module inverse images are exact, and $D^+$ means the derived category of complexes whose cohomology vanishes in sufficiently negative degrees [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; on $BG$ sections and their derived functor are invariants and continuous cohomology [def-exc-continuous-cohomology]. Write
$$a_K:R\Gamma(BG,K)\longrightarrow R\Gamma(E,\rho^*K)$$
for the canonical unit-induced comparison. There exists an $A$-linear triangulated functor $F:D^+(BG,A)\to D^+(A)$, with natural distinguished triangles
$$R\Gamma(BG,K)\xrightarrow{a_K}R\Gamma(E,\rho^*K)\longrightarrow F(K)\longrightarrow R\Gamma(BG,K)[1],$$
where triangulated has the meaning of [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Put $M=g'_*A$, namely the permutation module $\operatorname{Map}(Q,A)$ with translation action. There is a canonical sheaf isomorphism $g_*A\simeq\rho^*M$. The finite-cover direct images $g_*,g'_*$ are exact, and the natural derived-section identifications
$$R\Gamma(BG,M)\simeq R\Gamma(BH,A),\qquad R\Gamma(E,\rho^*M)\simeq R\Gamma(E',A)$$
carry $a_M$ to the unit-induced map $R\Gamma(BH,A)\to R\Gamma(E',A)$ for $\rho'$. In particular, $F(M)$ is a cone of that latter map. No purity hypothesis or conclusion is part of this statement.

source.place: Expose XVI, paragraphs between Lemmas 3.4.8 and 3.4.9, printed pp.247–248: finite covering direct-image comparison and the triangulated relative cohomology functor. The general finite-slice formulation records precisely the topos argument used there.
